feedback.problem: Find the critical points of the function $f(x)=3{x}^{3}+12{x}^{2}+12x+13.$
feedback.worked_solution:
A critical point of $f(x)$ is a point $x=c$ in the domain of $f$ such that either ${f}^{′}(c)=0$ or ${f}^{′}(c)$ does not exist.

Differentiating $f(x),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{3}+12{x}^{2}+12x+13) \\  & =9{x}^{2}+24x+12.\end{aligned}
$$

We now proceed to find the critical points:

- First, we compute the points where ${f}^{′}(c)=0.$ We set the derivative equal to zero, and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9{x}^{2}+24x+12 & =0 \\ 3{x}^{2}+8x+4 & =0 \\ (3x+2)(x+2) & =0 \\ x & =-\frac{2}{3},\,-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)$ has stationary points at $x=-\frac{2}{3}$ and $x=-2.$

- Second, we note that ${f}^{′}(x)$ exists for all values of $x$ in the domain of $f(x).$ So $f(x)$ has no non-stationary critical points.

Therefore, we conclude that the critical points of $f(x)$ are $x=-\frac{2}{3}$ and $x=-2.$
